The data above is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z>0.33).$ Use the table above and do not round your answer.

$P(Z>0.33)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/597125714057269b7adf9c0a2a9bbdde9631cf37bc80518281ab4444c3189717.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1),$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>a)=P(Z<-a)=Φ(-a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z>0.33).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/98cc48cff914158a4c8facf34de162a237e07ba271067aa51ba719a66f17d8af.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z<-0.33).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/357a942bf0b8976c29eedb7f865c381a46c3f841eadfc2203ca3192cea8275af.png)

Therefore,

$$
P(Z>0.33)=P(Z<-0.33)=Φ(-0.33)=0.3707.
$$
